findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: G = ℤ₂ (the discrete group with two elements) is a non-trivial Polish group that is uniquely homogeneous, since |Homeo(ℤ₂)| = 2 and for any p, q ∈ ℤ₂ there is exactly one permutation/homeomorphism sending p to q; likewise, the trivial group with one element is also uniquely homogeneous (and Theorem 1.1 explicitly requires more than two elements for this reason). Thus Theorem 3.1 fails for the non-trivial Polish group G = ℤ₂ (and in the abstract p1-4 which claims there are no uniquely homogeneous Polish groups). In general, a uniquely homogeneous space X must have |Homeo(X)| = |X|, which holds for any space with 1 or 2 points.

evidence.text: Theorem 3.1. A non-trivial Polish group cannot be uniquely homogeneous.
